subs: Beds on its Medicare cost report. A licensed bed count usually runs higher.
Every intensive and special care unit counts: adult, cardiac, surgical, burn, neonatal and pediatric.
Each inpatient stay that ended counts once, whoever paid for it.
All inpatient days divided by discharges. Answer in days, like 4.5.
Patient days divided by the bed days it had available.
Medicare Advantage plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Medicaid managed care plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payroll only: not clinics, not contract staff.
Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.
From AHRQ's 2023 list of who owns which hospital, matched to Medicare's hospital list.
Small rural hospitals with 25 inpatient beds at most, paid by Medicare on their costs.
By the county each hospital sits in, as CMS records it.
Every one of its hospitals' latest Medicare cost report, added up.
Biggest by beds on its cost report. The answer names the hospital.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payrolls only: clinics, offices and any health plan are left out.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Medical Center have on its payroll in 2024?
questions.why: No other Garnet Health hospital reports more; Medical Center Catskills (Harris) is next at 466. About 8.3 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Medical Center Catskills (Harris) have on its payroll in 2024?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Garnet Health hospitals; Medical Center has the most, 2,733. About 6.1 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Medical Center Catskills (Callicoon) have on its payroll in 2024?
questions.why: That is the fewest of 3 Garnet Health hospitals; Medical Center has the most, 2,733. About 2.5 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent resident physicians trained at Medical Center in 2024?
questions.why: Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees do Garnet Health's hospitals have on payroll, added together?
questions.why: From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent resident physicians train in Garnet Health's hospitals, added together?
questions.why: One of its hospitals reports residents; Medical Center trains the most, 97.

questions.q: What percent of Medical Center's inpatient days in 2024 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Garnet Health hospitals; Medical Center Catskills (Callicoon) runs highest, 69 percent. Traditional Medicare was 38 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 25 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Medical Center Catskills (Harris)'s inpatient days in 2024 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: That is the lowest of 3 Garnet Health hospitals; Medical Center Catskills (Callicoon) runs highest, 69 percent. Traditional Medicare was 39 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 21 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Medical Center Catskills (Callicoon)'s inpatient days in 2024 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: No other Garnet Health hospital runs higher; Medical Center is next at 63 percent. Traditional Medicare was 68 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 2 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Medical Center's inpatient days in 2024 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicaid was 5 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 11 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Medical Center Catskills (Harris)'s inpatient days in 2024 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicaid was 5 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 17 percent.

questions.q: Across all of Garnet Health's hospitals, what percent of inpatient days were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: Across every U.S. hospital's cost report it is 44 percent.

questions.q: Across all of Garnet Health's hospitals, what percent of inpatient days were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Across every U.S. hospital's cost report it is 24 percent.

questions.why: That is 15 percent of its 329 beds.

questions.q: How many intensive care beds did Medical Center Catskills (Harris) report to Medicare for 2024?
questions.why: That is 13 percent of its 76 beds.

questions.q: How many hospitals does Garnet Health run, by the federal list of health systems?
questions.why: All of them are in New York. A system's own count can differ: it may count campuses on their own, or hospitals that joined after 2023.

questions.q: How many of Garnet Health's hospitals are critical access hospitals?
questions.why: They are Medical Center Catskills (Callicoon).

questions.q: How many of Garnet Health's hospitals are outside a metropolitan area?
questions.why: They are Medical Center Catskills (Callicoon) and Medical Center Catskills (Harris).

questions.q: How many beds do Garnet Health's hospitals report to Medicare, added together?
questions.why: From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.

questions.q: How many beds does Garnet Health's biggest hospital report to Medicare?
questions.why: It is Medical Center. Medical Center Catskills (Harris) is next, with 76.

questions.q: How many intensive care beds do Garnet Health's hospitals report to Medicare, added together?
questions.why: That is 14 percent of their 420 beds. From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.

questions.why: About 60 a day. From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.
